answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a saffron, before it can post or attest. A single grove checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 125 aliases thus costs 54 bonds held for 14 days each, plus the pearl attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
